Meta.title: Video Dub — Real-time video dubbing in your browser
Meta.description: A Chrome extension that dubs any subtitled video in real time — French, Spanish, Italian, German or Portuguese. Local translation, synced speech, zero setup.

Hero.title: Watch any course in <accent>your language</accent>
Hero.subtitle: Video Dub is a Chrome extension that dubs subtitled videos in real time. It rebuilds full sentences from the captions, translates them locally, and speaks over the video — perfectly in sync.
Hero.note: Works on any player that exposes a subtitle track — including custom course platforms.

Features.title: Built like a real dubbing studio
Features.subtitle: Not a robotic caption reader. Video Dub reconstructs sentences, keeps one consistent voice, and adapts its pace to the speaker.

sentences.title: Full-sentence dubbing
sentences.description: Caption fragments are merged into complete sentences before translation, so the voice flows naturally and translations keep their context.

local.title: Local translation
local.description: Uses Chrome's built-in on-device translation API first — free, private and offline-friendly — with an online fallback when unavailable.

sync.title: Always in sync
sync.description: Speech follows the video clock: pause, seek or replay and the voice follows instantly. Gentle rate adaptation keeps long sentences intelligible.

voices.title: One consistent voice
voices.description: A single voice is picked per session for coherence. Choose any installed system voice, including premium natural voices on macOS.

overlay.title: Floating controls
overlay.description: A draggable on-page controller lets you toggle dubbing, switch language, adjust speed and duck the original audio without leaving the video.

languages.title: Five languages
languages.description: Dub English videos into French, Spanish, Italian, German or Portuguese. Switching languages mid-video is instant and never mixes voices.

detect.title: Detects the video
detect.description: The extension finds the video player on the page — even inside shadow DOM players like Mux — and reads its English subtitle track.

translate.title: Translates ahead
translate.description: Upcoming sentences are translated ahead of playback with Chrome's local translation model, cached per language.

speak.title: Speaks over the video
speak.description: A synthesized voice speaks each sentence at the right moment while the original audio is automatically lowered.

Install.title: Install in two minutes
Install.subtitle: Video Dub is not on the Chrome Web Store yet — install it as an unpacked extension.

clone.title: Get the code
clone.description: Clone the repository or download it as a ZIP, then keep the extension folder somewhere permanent.

load.title: Load it in Chrome
load.description: Open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, click “Load unpacked” and select the extension folder.

play.title: Play a video
play.description: Open any subtitled video, let it play for a few seconds, then flip the switch in the popup or the floating bar.

Install.storeSoon: Coming soon to the Chrome Web Store

sites.question: Which sites does it work on?
sites.answer: Any site whose player exposes a subtitle or caption track — course platforms, documentation videos, most custom HTML5 players. If the player draws captions without a text track, dubbing is not possible yet.

cost.question: Is it really free?
cost.answer: Yes. Translation runs on-device with Chrome's built-in API (Chrome 138+) and speech uses your system's voices. No account, no API key, no quota.

voice.question: Can I improve the voice quality?
voice.answer: Yes — install higher-quality system voices. On macOS: System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → download a premium voice for your language, then pick it in the popup.

privacy.question: What about privacy?
privacy.answer: Subtitles are translated locally whenever Chrome's on-device model is available. Only when it isn't, sentences are sent to an online translation fallback. Nothing else ever leaves your browser.

youtube.question: How is this different from YouTube auto-dubbing?
youtube.answer: YouTube's dubbing only exists on YouTube. Video Dub brings the same experience — full-sentence translation, one voice, ducked original audio — to any site with subtitles.

Footer.tagline: Real-time video dubbing in your browser.
